title: Microsoft Just Cut 4,800 Jobs to Pay for AI. Its 20,000 Indian Employees Are Watching.
excerpt: The company's fourth round of layoffs in eighteen months guts the Xbox division and deepens a pattern that is sending thousands of Indian tech workers home from the US.
body:
Microsoft announced on Monday that it would cut 4,800 jobs — roughly 2.1 per cent of its global workforce — overhauling its Xbox gaming business and trimming commercial teams as it redirects billions of dollars toward artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The restructuring is the company's fourth significant headcount action in eighteen months. It follows voluntary buyouts offered to about 9,000 employees earlier this year under a controversial "Rule of 70" formula, and comes after Microsoft's shares recorded their worst first-half performance since 2022, falling nearly 23 per cent.

## Xbox Gets a Hard Reset

The sharpest cuts fall inside the gaming division, where 3,200 positions will be eliminated, with 1,600 employees let go immediately. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who took over from 38-year veteran Phil Spencer in February, described the division's trajectory as unsustainable.

"Excluding Activision Blizzard King, over the past five years, we have spent over $20 billion on ongoing investments in our content, platform and hardware subsidy, but our annual revenue has declined nearly half a billion during that time," Sharma wrote in a memo published on Microsoft's website. "Going forward, this cannot continue."


![Hard Reset — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/c/c2/Hard_Reset_cover.jpg)



> **"Amazon and Meta Platforms have also cut thousands of positions this year as the industry's historic AI outlays — set to top $700 billion in 2026 — pressure companies to demonstrate returns."**



The restructuring will see four studios either spun off or made independent — Compulsion Games, Double Fine Productions, Ninja Theory, and Undead Labs — while French studio Arkane has begun consultations with its workers' union. Microsoft is also considering a potential spinoff of the entire Xbox unit, a dramatic admission that its $69 billion Activision Blizzard acquisition has not closed the gap with Sony's PlayStation or Nintendo.

## The AI Spending Squeeze

The layoffs are part of a broader pattern across Big Tech. Amazon and Meta Platforms have also cut thousands of positions this year as the industry's historic AI outlays — set to top $700 billion in 2026 — pressure companies to demonstrate returns.

Microsoft's Chief People Officer Amy Coleman told employees that the eliminated roles "are not being replaced by AI," but acknowledged that AI is fundamentally reshaping how work gets done. Analysts see the cuts differently. "Microsoft has been managing down its workforce in order to pay for its AI investments," said Gil Luria, managing director of D.A. Davidson. "By keeping its headcount down they have been able to accelerate revenue growth while maintaining the same margins."

The company's Azure cloud-computing business, once the exclusive seller of OpenAI's models, continues to see booming demand. But its $190 billion spending projection for 2026 has raised questions about whether even Microsoft's balance sheet can absorb the capital requirements of the AI era indefinitely.


![Asha Sharma — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/62/Asha_Sharma_CEO_of_XBOX_at_2026_XBOX_Showcase.jpg)


## What This Means for Indian Tech Workers

Microsoft employs more than 20,000 people across India — in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, New Delhi, Mumbai, Pune, and Chennai — spanning engineering, AI, cloud, sales, support, and operations. The company has not confirmed whether Indian offices will be affected by this round.

India may be partly insulated: Microsoft announced a $3 billion investment in the country in 2025 to expand AI and cloud infrastructure, and engineering and cloud roles are generally considered safer than the sales and consulting positions that took the heaviest cuts.

But the broader trend is unmistakable. According to tracking data, over 122,000 tech workers have been laid off globally in 2026, with AI cited as the primary driver. For Indian professionals on H-1B and L-1 visas in the United States, each layoff round restarts a brutal 60-day clock to find new sponsorship or leave the country. The pattern has fuelled a growing "reverse migration" trend, with over 15,000 Indian tech professionals returning home in 2025 alone, according to staffing firm Xpheno.

The cuts also ripple through India's IT services ecosystem. As American companies reduce onshore headcount and push more work offshore, Indian IT firms like TCS and Infosys face a paradox: more outsourced work, but at a time when their own workforces are under pressure from AI automation.

Microsoft's stock fell 1.5 per cent in early Monday trading. The company is expected to report quarterly results later this month.
